Arguable the best 40K video game both past, present and future since it is unlikely the 40K universe is ever going to see THQ level of money put into it again.  Space Marine is a third-person shooter/melee game set in Games Workshop's flagship setting Warhammer 40,000.  You take the role of Captain Titus.  One of the few Ultramarines (a chapter of post human super-soldier warrior monks) who sees the Codex Astartes (the rules that Space Marines or Adeptus Astartes follow concerning how to conduct war) as a set of guidelines and not immutable facts.  The Ultramarines are sent to a forge world (planet devoted to the manufacture of technology mostly weapons) that is under attack by an Ork invasion.

The game play of Space Marine feels faithful to the source material as you place a seven foot tall superhuman in power armor wielding guns that basically fire grenades.  Meaning that your character and weapons feels heavy but not sluggish.  Both being very satisfying.  Unlike many games of the time, Space Marine avoid chest high walls of the other cover shooters of the time.  Instead it has the player rely on rolls and moving in and out out cover.  Space Marine has fairly unique health system with half your health being basically shield that recharge over time (fairly typical of the era) while the other half can only be regained via special melee kill attacks.  This forces the player to engage in Space Marine's melee combat system which while basic, I found quite good.  To break up game play a little bit, some parts of the story mode has Captain Titus don a jump pack which allows him to soar through the air smashing into his foes below in a thunderous attack.  I found the jump pack portions very fun especially when armed with a Thunderhammer (a two-handed lightning maul).

While the enemy AI is basic, I appreciate the fact that the orks would sometimes make a quick head dip motion just as I would be ready to make my head shot.  I found enemy animations to sometimes be pretty wily dodging my bolter fire if I became complacent.  If I had to fault anything, I would say the orks were far better shots than I was led to believe in the tabletop game.  If I had one complaint about this game, it would be that the final boss fight quick-time-event action was underwhelming and a little bit out of place since it didn't really happen anywhere else save winning melee attacks against a few of the stronger enemies.  But that was only the very end of the game and quite forgivable.

All in all, Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine is a good third-person shooter that fans of the setting and action-shooters will enjoy.  I will admit that without the setting it isn't anything special other than competent/good game.  I remember playing the demo when it originally came out since a few of my friends at the time were really into 40k.  I didn't know much about the setting so I found the demo fine but not nearly engaging enough to even spend half the asking price brand new.  Now has a fan of 40k, I found the game far more enjoyable and very worth picking up.
